brief.ask: Create a brand identity for Seamline, the open-source command-line tool in this folder.
brief.owner: Owner preferences: precise, trustworthy, developer-native; it must work in a terminal-heavy README, as a GitHub avatar and on a small docs site. No database cylinders, no elephants, no generic terminal prompt. Web and GitHub only.

claim.notes: Only mirror-s passed the gate (avg 6.77, after two rework rounds); shift and overlap were rejected at sketch review, and originality is insufficient-evidence with no registry search done, so trademark clearance is still open.

concepts.title: Reversible s
readsAs: letter S built from two hooks
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 coin/disc cut by a staircase zigzag, faint S; s2 bitten block plus wedge; s3 pixel mountain/graph silhouette; s4 square frame/window icon. Pick s1: only one with a seam you can name, survives 16 px. Keep the stepped cut, make the S reading deliberate and the halves less coin-like; avoid sync/refresh icon feel.

concepts.title: Handoff
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 pie chart; s2 chat bubble/app tile; s3 leaf/flag shapes; s4 tadpole/sperm; s5 pizza slice with eclipse or Pac-Man. Strike all: stock or off-message, overlap tiles mostly read as generic. Try a more constructed, geometric overlap not built from blobs and wedges.

concepts.title: Live seam
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 digit 2 or S/5; s2 division sign; s3 easing-curve/S icon; s4 prohibited/no-sign. All struck as a different letter, UI icon or stock shape. Try a form that is not a letter or stroke: one distinctive notched or offset construction.
